clinician.final_diagnosis: a presumptive diagnosis of stage IV adenoid cystic carcinoma with metastases to the liver and lung was made
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old male presented with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and early satiety. Initial CT showed a large 14 cm left hepatic lobe mass with hepatomegaly. Laboratory tests revealed mild transaminase elevation and normal tumor markers. A liver biopsy was ordered but histopathology results were not documented. Subsequent chest CT imaging revealed innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules suggestive of metastases. Follow-up abdominal CT angiography showed growth of the hepatic mass to 21 cm, consistent with progressive disease. The clinical scenario with imaging and laboratory findings led to a presumptive diagnosis of stage IV adenoid cystic carcinoma with liver and lung metastases.
